question.leadin: After this battle, Pheidippides ran approximately 26 miles to Athens to announce a Greek victory.
question.text: Name this 490 BCE battle that lends its name to a very long race.
question.clue: The retreating side in this battle traveled towards Mesogia and attempted to escape on their triremes, where some of them drowned in a swamp after getting pincered.

swap.leadin: The Phaistos Disc, an artifact found in one of this civilization's palaces, may represent an undeciphered writing system.
swap.text: Name this ancient civilization from the island of Crete, which also developed the Linear A writing system.
swap.clue: A devastating blow this civilization occurred when the Thera volcano erupted in the 16th century BCE, which contributed to their eventual decline and the occupation by the Mycenaean Greeks.

question.leadin: Answer the following about historians of the ancient world.
question.text: Despite telling tales of giant ants and massive armies, this Greek is known as the "Father of Histories" for his work the Histories, which details the Persian Wars in addition to providing interesting if not accurate ethnographies of various classical peoples.
question.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

swap.leadin: -- give the following about classical historians.
swap.text: This Athenian general included Pericles' funeral oration in book two of his History of the Peloponnesian War.
swap.clue: Part of his work involved character studies of Brasidas, Cleon, and Themistocles, and he described the disastrous siege of Syracuse and the funeral oration of Pericles.

question.leadin: The first half of this war ended with the signing of the Peace of Nicias.
question.text: Name this 5th century BCE war, fought for almost thirty years, between Athens and Sparta.
question.clue: During this conflict, a general noted that "honor is the delight of men when they are old and useless" as part of a set of remarks that are sometimes attributed to his consort.

swap.text: The formalization of the Athenian class system as property-based and the relaxation of Draco's harsh laws are credited to this early 6th-century reformer, one of the Seven Sages of Greece.
swap.clue: After promulgating his laws on wooden tablets, this ruler left on a series of journeys.

question.leadin: This leader may have been killed when a roof tile was thrown at him during the Battle of Argos.
question.text: Name this Greek ruler who was taken hostage and forced to marry Ptolemy I's daughter Antigone. This king of Epirus complained "another such victory and we are undone" while campaigning in Italy.
question.clue: The Romans renamed the town of Maleventum to Beneventum after this man fought there on behalf of Tarentum.

swap.text: During this campaign, Alcibiades was recalled to stand trial on charges that he had desecrated the Hermai statues, prompting him to flee to Sparta. A lunar eclipse convinced his replacement, Nicias, not to retreat when things went sour.
swap.clue: Those losers surrendered to Gylippus a year after Lamachus's death.

question.text: Ranked number one was this man, victor of Granicus, Issus, Arbela, and Hydaspes before his early death in 323 BCE.
question.clue: This man-rejecting the advice of Parmenio-decided then not to attack at night.

swap.leadin: This period marks the second of three devised by Christian Jurgensen Thomsen.
swap.text: Name this period of human history, during which England's Wessex culture developed and the Minoan civilization flourished. The Greek Dark Ages began after the collapse of the civilizations from this period.
swap.clue: Earlier in this time period, Greece had been home to the Minoans.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the early Dark Ages.
question.text: Historians look at the "migration" of people known by this term, which included the Huns and Ostrogoths. The Romans used this term to refer to the "uncivilized" tribes of people living outside their borders.
question.clue: A word that is probably derived from the Greek word rha plus the Greek root of this word is traditionally used by stage actors to imitate the sound of indistinct conversation.

swap.text: The first businessman to become leader of Athens was this rival of Pericles who defeated Sparta at Sphacteria but was later killed at Amphipolis by Brasidas.
swap.clue: In that play, the Paphlagonian oracle is stolen by two slaves who depict this man's political contemporaries Nicias and Demosthenes.

question.text: The Persians intend to reinstate this son of Pisistratus and brother of Hipparchus as tyrant of Athens. Prior to Marathon, he had a dream in which he slept with his mother, which he wrongly believed to foretell his return to Athens.
question.clue: This son of Pisistratus ruled as a tyrant in Athens before being overthrown by Cleisthenes, thus beginning the period of Athenian democracy. This ruler's brother, Hipparchus, was killed by Harmodius and Aristogeiton.

swap.leadin: Thasos tried to leave this alliance after a dispute over gold mines.
swap.text: Name this alliance of city-states which dissolved as a result of the Peloponnesian War.
swap.clue: Though this organization's nominal purpose was to oppose Persian aggression, its power was centralized after its treasury was moved from its namesake island to the mainland- specifically, into the Parthenon.

question.leadin: Emmett Bennett's standardization efforts helped the completion of this task, which was met with initial skepticism until scholars examined the tripod tablet uncovered by Carl Blegen.
question.text: Name this task completed by Michael Ventris, who published a monograph on its results with John Chadwick. Objects found at Tiryns and Pylos helped complete this task.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the economic history of the successor rump states that emerged from the 1204 Sack of Constantinople.
swap.text: It's not the Morea, but religious silver coins were produced by the mint at Arta that operated under the "Despotate" of this ancient region of western Greece and Albania. Home to the oracle at Dodona, this region's Molossians were led by a king who defeated Rome at Heraclea and Asculum.
swap.clue: That king of this region ignored his advisor Cineas and came to the aid of Tarentum, leading to a defeat at Beneventum.

question.text: The Panhellenic colony of Thurii (thoo-ree-"eye") was established at the direction of Pericles in this larger region. This term refers to colonies like Croton and Sybaris that first brought Greek culture to southern Italy and Sicily.
question.clue: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in a city in this region.

swap.text: Troops from this city were the only ones to help Athens at the Battle of Marathon. According to Herodotus, Aristides ("air-ih-STY-deez") the Just led Athenian forces at a battle near this city that was honored with the "Serpent Column."
swap.clue: This city's strategic position came from its overlooking the road from Thebes to Corinth.

question.text: The first half of the war is named for this king of Sparta, who in Thucydides gives a speech advising the Spartans not to start the war in the first place.

swap.leadin: An army trapped on this island sent messengers to the mainland, who returned with the message that "the Spartans order you to make your own decision about yourselves, so long as you do nothing dishonorable."
swap.text: Name this island off the Peloponnesian coast where Spartan warriors surrendered for the first time in 425 BCE.
swap.clue: One of Cleon's bright spots was his blockade and capture of this island and the 440 Spartan hoplites on it in 425 BC. It was part of the larger Battle of Pylos
